A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Stand-In and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. The method, experiments, and relocated appendix content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original quantitative comparisons, a 20-participant user study, component ablations, and generated-video examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains the quantitative comparisons and user study and reports revised ablations, attention visualizations, and additional qualitative generalization results.

M1.justification: The Wan2.1-based conditional image branch, image-QKV LoRA, restricted attention, disjoint positional mapping, fixed reference timestep, and KV caching remain unchanged. Equations 1–4 and Algorithm 1 are retained. VSA and SPM are experimental alternatives, not changes to the proposed model.

E1.justification: V3 adds explicitly presented qualitative evaluation on unseen ordinary individuals across age and ethnicity, including elderly Asian and Black subjects and children (Figures 9 and 19). The 2,000-video training dataset and existing human, non-human, pose-guided, stylization, and face-swapping tasks remain.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain the same external comparators; ConcatID-WAN-AdaLN is shortened to ConcatID-WAN with identical scores. Within the ablation comparisons, however, v1's LoRA-removal and positional-mapping-removal variants are replaced by bidirectional vanilla self-attention and shared-position-mapping variants.

E3.justification: The reported training settings, primary metrics, and 20-participant/10-video user-study protocol remain unchanged. The ablation design changes its attention and positional controls, and Table 3 drops the prompt-following metric. The new attention analysis averages maps across DiT blocks.

E4.justification: The central component ablations are substantially redesigned around RSA versus VSA and CPM versus SPM. V3 adds attention-concentration and spatial-layout analyses (Figures 5–6), replaces the appendix ablation examples, removes the combined-removal example, and adds demographic generalization analysis (Section 9 and Figure 19).

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The user-study averaging procedure and participant/video counts are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain identical scores. Table 3 replaces the old controls' face-similarity/naturalness results, 0.022/3.528 and 0.021/3.539, with 0.422/3.855 for VSA and 0.536/3.755 for SPM under different conditions. Ablation prompt-following scores disappear. Mechanistic and demographic examples are added, while v1's girl-painting comparison is removed.

T1.justification: The positional-coordinate definitions and attention equations remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version provides theorems or proofs; the added explanations concern empirical behavior and mechanism interpretation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the central claims: lightweight identity control using approximately 1% additional parameters and 2,000 training pairs, strong generation performance, and plug-and-play applicability. Greater emphasis on preserving pretrained priors explains these retained claims without redefining the contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations linking VSA to diffuse background attention and identity drift, and shared coordinates to disrupted positional priors and distorted facial geometry (Sections 3.2–3.3, 4.5, and 8). Section 9 also interprets the new examples as evidence of generalization across demographic variation.

D1.justification: V3 replaces the introductory project-website reference with a GitHub repository link on the title page, documents attention-map averaging, and supplies prompts for the new generalization examples. LoRA rank, hardware, training steps, batch size, preprocessing, and inference pseudocode remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning beyond the earlier video-focused discussion to subject-specific fine-tuning and zero-shot image personalization. Added works include Textual Inversion, DreamBooth, InstantID, PuLID, and IP-Adapter, alongside additional video-generation literature and references for existing evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: Rewriting concentrates on the RSA/CPM rationale and ablation discussion, while much existing prose remains. V3 introduces numbered subsections, renames the framework subsection, moves pseudocode to the beginning of the supplement, removes its contents page, and updates the author and affiliation block.

P2.justification: V3 adds mechanism and demographic figures, replaces the appendix ablation display, and removes one qualitative comparison. Table 1 changes from a full-width table with an open-source column to a single-column table with source-type groups; Table 3 loses a metric column. The document template and placement of numerous retained figures and tables also change.

improvement.justification: V1's RSA ablation removed LoRA, whereas v3 directly compares restricted and bidirectional attention. Together with attention maps and spatial examples, this better supports assessment of the design rationale; expanded related work improves context. The gains are limited: primary benchmark and user-study results remain unchanged, demographic evidence is qualitative, and ablation prompt-following scores and one comparison case are lost.
